items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: And I think at that time Camille Howard, of course, was with Roy Milton at the time.

ctx.x: Yeah. And so then the area was empty, and so part of the neighborhood became black and became referred to as Bronzeville, and it was during that period that Shep's Playhouse opened and had jazz, was the way it was told to me. Is that right?

Bronzeville, yeah. I can't remember. It wasn't -- Bronzeville wasn't the real popular name for it. They called it another section, a section I can't think of. I can't even remember what they called it at the time. However, there were many breakfast clubs up in there at the time, and Shep's Playhouse of course was a regular nightclub, and a fantastic, beautiful place. A beautiful nightclub. And let me see, Roy Milton worked -- he worked in that area. He worked at a club there. And I think at that time Camille…
But that whole area was really --
